rows.accepted_claim: For a finite declared Cell model (X,C), non-overlapping occupied sets are exactly independent sets of the conflict graph; optimum occupancy is alpha(G)/|X|.
rows.hypothesis_comparison: External conflict-graph encoding assumes only a finite object set plus pairwise incompatibility. The P000 pressure-test adds Cell typing but no stronger mathematics once C is declared.
rows.consequence: Do not continue this as a new Packing theorem; novelty can only enter through the choice/derivation of the native conflict relation C.

rows.accepted_claim: T_n=(Z/nZ)^6 with ±e_i conflict, even n>=4, is a 12-regular bipartite torus with parity classes.
rows.hypothesis_comparison: This graph is exactly the even k-ary n-cube Q_6^n (notation swapped: alphabet size n, dimension 6), i.e. Cartesian product of six even cycles. Even-k bipartiteness and parity coloring are standard.
rows.consequence: The declared torus is a standard network/Cayley graph, not a new native geometric object.

rows.hypothesis_comparison: A finite regular bipartite graph has equal color classes and, by Hall, a perfect matching. One color class gives N/2 independent vertices and the perfect matching gives alpha<=N/2. This applies to every regular bipartite graph, strictly more general than the six-axis torus.
rows.consequence: The exact 1/2 optimum is a special case of classical matching/bipartite theory.

rows.accepted_claim: The spectral certificate with degree d=12 and least adjacency eigenvalue tau=-12 yields alpha/N<=1/2.
rows.hypothesis_comparison: The return uses Hoffman's ratio bound in its standard form alpha/N <= -tau/(d-tau), with the torus eigenvalues substituted.
rows.consequence: The spectral proof is a textbook/existing bound application, useful as independent certification but not new.

rows.accepted_claim: For a periodic lift from a finite-index quotient of Z^6, every Følner sequence sees density |I|/|Q|.
rows.hypothesis_comparison: Johnson–McClendon Lemma 2.7 proves the stronger coset statement for any Følner sequence in Z^d and any finite-index subgroup: each coset has limiting proportion 1/[Z^d:G]. Summing the occupied cosets gives the P000 declared-model theorem immediately.
rows.consequence: The density theorem is classical amenable-group/coset equidistribution once a translation action is supplied.

rows.accepted_claim: Finite-window discrepancy from a periodic packing is confined to incomplete fundamental tiles; parity packing has |2|P∩W|-|W||<=b_M(W).
rows.hypothesis_comparison: Both are finite boundary decompositions of a periodic/fundamental-domain or perfect-matching partition. Complete blocks contribute exactly their fixed quota; only boundary-crossing blocks contribute error. The external framework is more general than the specific parity packing.
rows.consequence: Boundary-error bookkeeping is standard; no successor should be opened by varying the window shape.

rows.accepted_claim: For q_{k,n}:T_{kn}->T_n, full inverse images of independent sets are independent and equal k^6 fibers preserve occupancy exactly.
rows.hypothesis_comparison: For any graph homomorphism, the inverse image of an independent set is independent. The extra density equality is immediate from the declared constant fiber size k^6. The general homomorphism statement has weaker hypotheses than this torus quotient.
rows.consequence: Finite refinement pullback is standard graph-homomorphism plus counting; only a physical/native interpretation of q can be new.

rows.accepted_claim: Translations and the realized carrier-S4 coordinate permutations preserve conflict and optimum occupancy; parity may be fixed or swapped.
rows.hypothesis_comparison: Graph automorphisms preserve adjacency and therefore independent sets/alpha. The S4 calculation is a standard finite group action on coordinate labels.
rows.consequence: No native rotation theorem follows merely from automorphism invariance of the declared carrier model.

rows.accepted_claim: The accepted carrier S4 has 24 elements; the orbit of direction label AB has size 6 and stabilizer size 4.
rows.hypothesis_comparison: Orbit-stabilizer gives |Orb(AB)|=|S4|/|Stab(AB)|=24/4=6 once the action is declared.
rows.consequence: This is standard group-action bookkeeping, not a new direction theorem.

rows.accepted_claim: For finitely many paths with linearly independent direction vectors, the bipartite incidence graph between paths and multiply-covered Cells is a forest.
rows.hypothesis_comparison: A simple incidence cycle supplies nonzero displacements along its participating paths whose signed sum is zero; hence it produces a nontrivial linear dependence among the distinct direction vectors. Therefore linear independence forbids every Berge/incidence cycle. This argument works for any number p of independent directions, not specifically six.
rows.consequence: The forest lemma is an elementary linear-algebra/Berge-acyclic consequence and generalizes immediately to p directions.

rows.accepted_claim: For six independent equal-length-r paths, overlap defect D=sum_x(m_x-1)<=5; K_6(r)=6r-5; equality iff overlap incidence is connected.
rows.hypothesis_comparison: For p path-nodes, q shared-cell nodes and c components in an incidence forest, E=(p+q)-c and D=E-q=p-c. Hence |union|=pr-D=pr-p+c>=pr-p+1. A connected realization has c=1 and equality. The accepted formula is the p=6 specialization, so the antecedent is strictly more general.
rows.consequence: Any successor proving K_p(r)=pr-p+1 under the same forest hypothesis, changing 6 to d, or restating equality-connectedness is killed as classical/elementary duplication.

rows.accepted_claim: A non-concurrent r=2 equality chain attains support 7, showing equality does not require six-way concurrency.
rows.hypothesis_comparison: Forest Euler counting predicts that every connected incidence tree has the same defect p-1, but external graph theory does not by itself certify that a particular typed coordinate chain is realizable in the project carrier. The exact coordinate witness is model-specific, while its cardinality consequence is standard.
rows.consequence: Retain only as a regression witness against an overstrong equality characterization, not as a standalone theorem frontier.

rows.accepted_claim: The dependent direction family {e1,e2,e1+e2} admits an incidence cycle and an r=2 packet with support 3, below the independent-axis forest value 4.
rows.hypothesis_comparison: In the vector matroid the three directions form a circuit because e1+e2-(e1+e2)=0 and every proper pair is independent. Matroid/Berge theory predicts that dependence is exactly where a cycle obstruction can appear, but it does not determine the project-specific support-3 coordinate witness.
rows.consequence: The exact witness is useful only as a boundary detector; progress requires a native mixed/refining direction family, not more fixed-carrier circuit examples.

rows.accepted_claim: The fixed-six-axis support problem is a 'Kakeya' comparison target.
rows.hypothesis_comparison: Finite-field Kakeya requires a line in every direction of F_q^d and studies global lower bounds of order q^d. The accepted project theorem uses six selected independent finite paths of length r in a declared carrier window. Neither the direction quantifier, ambient algebra, nor objective matches.
rows.consequence: Classical Kakeya literature is context/analogy only; it is not an antecedent for K_6(r)=6r-5. Conversely, the name 'Kakeya' does not create novelty.

novelty_guard: NO novelty inference is permitted from NO_MATERIAL_MATCH or ADJACENT_METHOD; these labels only classify located antecedents under this audit.
